messages:
anna: Heads-up — after the runtime merge yesterday I'm seeing sporadic output corruption on long-context generation when activation quantization (FP8) is enabled. Only shows up on mixed-precision matmul stacks. Repro below.

jamal: ugh, any OOMs or NaNs?

anna: No OOM. Sometimes tokens are just wrong / logits explode for a step then recover. No consistent seed but much more frequent past 4096 seq_len.

maria: can you paste the minimal repro and the config you used?

anna: repro: 
```bash
RUNTIME_ARGS=\"--activation-quant=fp8 --mix-prec=bf16_fp8 --kernel-selector=auto\" 
./bin/run_inference --model redwood-open-3b --seq_len 8192 --prompt-file tiny_prompt.txt
```
log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-17T14:23:01Z] INFO kernel: selected kernel bf16_matmul_fast
[2026-03-17T14:23:01Z] WARN quant: activation scale mismatch detected (0.00012 vs 0.0021)
[2026-03-17T14:23:01Z] ERROR runtime: fp8_dequant produced NaN at out[512]
[2026-03-17T14:23:02Z] INFO runtime: recovered using fallback bf16 path
```

kevin: interesting — kernel selector picked bf16_matmul_fast then a dequant path ran? that WARN suggests scale bookkeeping for cached KV/partial prefixes is inconsistent.

sophia: could be a race between KV cache reuse and the quant calibration we added in the batching patch. If the per-request scale gets overwritten by prefix-scoring batch, dequant can use stale scale.

anna: bisect shows last good commit is 0x7c9a5 (pre batching heuristics tweak). suspect interaction between per-batch calibration and dynamic kernel flip.

jamal: @kevin can you dump the KV meta (scales + seq offsets) when this triggers? put to /tmp/kv-debug/<ts>. We need exact numbers to see if scale mismatch is coming from prefix vs suffix.

kevin: dumped a few runs: attached (pasted below).
```
KV_META: {layer:5, head:12, kv_scale: 0.000120, cached_prefix_scale: 0.002100, prefix_len: 4096, cur_seq_offset: 4096}
KV_META: {layer:5, head:12, kv_scale: 0.002100, cached_prefix_scale: 0.002100, prefix_len: 2048, cur_seq_offset: 2048}
```

maria: that first line is the smoking gun — kv_scale used by activations is 0.000120 but the cached prefix expects 0.002100. dequant uses kv_scale -> underflow -> NaN.

sophia: my hypothesis: when kernel-selector toggles from bf16_matmul_fast to fp8_matmul_smallseq for short tails, we don't persist per-head scale states correctly across the kernel boundary. the calibration routine writes into a local buffer that isn't flushed to KV meta on kernel change.

jamal: hotfix idea: disable activation-FP8 for sequences > 4096 or force a single kernel path for calls that touch cached prefixes until we fix scale state persistence. quick revert may be safer.

anna: agreed. a soft-fallback: if cached_prefix_scale / kv_scale > 10 || < 0.1 log and force fallback to bf16 path. That would avoid NaNs.

kevin: i'll prototype guard in kernel selector: if kv.cache_hit && activation_quant.enabled then require kernel.stable_across_prefixes == true. else force bf16.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy 2026-03-17T15:00 initiated for runtime v3.14.2-hotfix (no FP8 activations for big-seqs). Monitoring.

sophia: also add an assert in dequant that checks scale sanity and prints full per-head scales when mismatch > 5x. don't crash, fallback to bf16.

maria: after adding the guard + assert, I ran our 10k long-seq fuzz and haven't hit corruption in 6 hours. performance impact looks ~+3% latency for some tails.

anna: that's acceptable for now. create PR and flag in changelog: "temporary disable fp8 activation for cached-prefix paths; guard against scale mismatch". open issue for proper state flush across kernel boundary.

jamal: filing issue #4521 with repro, logs, and suggested root cause (kernel boundary scale persistence). assigning to runtime/quant-team.

kevin: PR up: https://git.company/repo/pulls/789 - includes guarded selector and improved dequant sanity logs.

maria: thanks team. next steps: 1) keep canary for 24h, 2) add unit test that simulates kernel flip with KV overlap, 3) plan a proper fix to persist per-head scale on kernel changes.

anna: I'll write the unit test case and runner. tagging @sophia for design review on persistent scale store.

sophia: on it. will post design doc draft in #eng-runtime-docs by EOD. :thumbsup:

anna: closing thread when canary 24h stable. thanks all.
